newsitem.title: UK: Softs Outlook - Coffee rally stalled, cocoa flags.
newsitem.headline: Softs Outlook - Coffee rally stalled, cocoa flags.

text.p: LIFFE coffee futures could see further retracement this week after a sell-off last week that slashed values by almost a third and took the steam out of the most explosive rally seen since early 1997.
Although traders said coffee was now technically oversold following last week's widespread profit-taking and long liquidation, there were no immediate signs that the market was hitting a bottom.

Elsewhere in soft commodities markets, cocoa was not yet clear of the danger of another setback while white sugar could be underpinned by perceptions of seasonal tightness into Europe's summer months.
Coffee's spectacular run-up since early January took a severe dent last week as speculators dumped positions to salvage some of their fast-diminishing profits.
Within a week, July delivery lost $855 per tonne, or 32 percent. It touched a low of $1,815 on Friday, the lowest since May 14, after hitting a 20-month high of $2,670 on May 29.
Traders said the fall was not unexpected as the rise had been too fast and too sharp.
They noted a vacuum between Friday's level and the next key support area at $1,680. "I don't think the market is really close to the bottom yet," said one.
While the immediate outlook hinged on talk of frost in Brazil, sentiment continued to be rattled by a deluge of bearish supply news -- led by Colombian sales.

In white sugar, the perception of seasonal tightness into Europe's summer months should keep nearby prices underpinned this week although sell orders at $330 and above should continue to cap gains on spot August.
"It's still reasonably tight," said one trader.
"There's more scale-up selling around than before, with people taking profits and trying to sell it around the $330 highs."
Traders said London's perceived strength should make the August/July arbitrage a buy at current levels as the New York market was expected to weaken.
Fund players in raws will have to liquidate hefty long July positions before expiry on June 30 and the nearby arbitrage was already attracting sellers keen for quick daily profits, they said.
"It (the arbitrage) is still holding quite well but there has been good selling on a daily basis," said another trader, citing slow upward progress.
Attention in London will centre on the July raws expiry as more South American sugar, particularly from Brazil's centre-south region, comes on stream.
But August whites should then take centre stage as some short players attempt to cover spot positions in the face of strong market prices, traders said.

In cocoa, traders said the market was not yet clear of the danger of another setback, although benchmark July had managed to avoid falling through crucial support at the April 9 low of 980 stg last week.
Traders saw July testing 980 once again, with more fund and speculator liquidation expected to emerge.
But floor sources said traders appeared to have underestimated fund and speculator longs in the London market last week.
Between 3,000 and 4,000 long positions were expected to be liquidated but the overall liquidation had been about double that amount, they said.

As the hefty liquidation had caught many players off guard, some traders speculated that a large long July holder had concealed some of its July rollovers amid the fund and speculator sales. Now they expected more sales.
If July breaks 980 stg, sell-stops should be triggered and attract fresh fund and speculator sales, traders said. That selling could force July down to about 950 before solid support surfaced.
